text: Vietnam isn't as easy a country to plan for as it appears online. The vibes of all three regions—North, Central, and South—are completely different. And if the itinerary isn't right, the entire trip can become unnecessarily hectic. In this video, I'll give you complete Vietnam itineraries for 9, 12, and 14 days. I'll also share details about flights, visas, transportation, food, stages, and budget. So, be sure to watch this video until the end. If you have nine days, this itinerary is a fairly balanced option, and I followed this route myself. So, guys, your trip starts in Hai. Day One: After checking into the hotel in Hanoi, exploring the Old Quarters is a great option. We went straight to the train station, and the vibe there was quite colorful and lively. Explore the cafes, try Vietnamese coffee, and slowly explore Hanoi's city life. Visiting the walking streets in the evening is definitely worth it. At night, this place completely transforms. Crowds are everywhere, live performances, and an energetic atmosphere reigns. Some people were even dancing on the streets . I even did a little bit of it. Overall, Day One is perfect for enjoying Hanoi's nightlife and local vibe. On Day Two, you can book an overnight cruise experience to Along Bay or Lana Bay. An early morning pickup from Hanoi for the overnight cruise takes around 2.5 to 3 hours. Then, you're transported to the cruise by small transfer boat. Upon arrival, the landscape changes drastically, with massive cliffs, limestone islands, and calm waters all around. Rooms are also quite premium, with private balconies with direct access. Activities like kayaking, cave exploration, and sunset deck views are all available for you to enjoy. The overnight cruise experience feels quite peaceful and luxurious. On Day Three, just like the cruise pick-up , they will drop you off in Haiphong. From Hanoi, take a bus to Sapa that night. Sapa is a hill station in Vietnam. The bus option is quite popular for reaching Sapa, as it's comparatively cheaper and more convenient. Sapa is around 300 kilometers from Haiphong, and the bus takes around 6 to 7 hours. As you move towards North Vietnam, both the weather and landscape change drastically. On Day Four, after arriving in Sapa, check into a pre-booked hotel. Pre-book a hotel so you can check in early and relax. Then, head to the Vet Trekking Cafe for breakfast. Here, along with coffee, you'll get an amazing view of the monorail passing through the rice terraces, which is seriously next-level . After that, explore Cat Cat Village. This is a traditional village where you can try local Vietnamese costumes and click amazing pictures. You can also enjoy waterfalls, cafes, and scenic trails. There's even a rainbow slide, which you can try. The atmosphere of the entire village is so aesthetic, it feels like you're walking through a movie set. In the evening, you can explore Sapa Town. Day 5 can be dedicated to Phan Pan, considered the highest peak in Indochina. But the destination isn't the only special thing; the journey to reach there is also quite adventurous. First, take a monorail that passes through rice terraces and valleys. Then, take a cable car ride, from where the entire landscape is visible in aerial view, with endless views of clouds and rice terraces all around. Then, another monorail takes you to the peak. The atmosphere of Phan Pan is quite unreal. Especially when the clouds move slowly. After Fancy Pan, you can go on an alpine coaster ride, which will make your entire experience even more adventurous. After a day of adventure, you can relax at night with a spa or massage. Then, take a bus from Sapa to Hanoi and stay near Hanoi's airport. Day Six: Take a morning flight from Hoi to Phuc. After the mountains and foggy landscapes of North Vietnam, Phuc offers a completely different vibe. The atmosphere here will be quite tropical and vibrant. Check into the hotel. After checking in at Sunset Town, you can explore the nearby cafes or simply take a walk. In the evening, the sunset from Kiss Bridge is beautiful, and the overall vibe is very romantic. There are also salsa and water performances. At night, you can also catch night shows like Symphony of the Sea and Kiss of the Sea. Water effects, slides, firecrackers, and even an ocean backdrop create a grand atmosphere. Don't miss these shows. In the morning of the day, you can experience the Hong Kong Cable Car ride, considered one of the world's longest sea cable cars. This cable car ride will drop you off on Hong Kong Island, where you can enjoy both a water park and a beach vibe. There are also numerous aesthetic cafes where you can chill out or have lunch. This island will easily fill half a day. In the evening, you can head to Grand World, approximately 40 to 45 minutes from Sunset Town. There are gondola rides, colorful streets, and night shows. Especially at night, the colorful lights and canals make the entire area feel like a mini Venice. On the day off, you can choose from two options depending on your mood and energy level. Option One: Whirlpool Safari and Wild Wonders. Early in the morning, you can head to Whirlpool Safari, which offers an open-air experience, allowing you to see animals up close and even feed some of them. Afterward, you can head to Whirlpool Wonders, also known as the Disneyland of Vietnam. It features water rides, roller coasters, various theme zones, and a large aquarium with mermaid shows . The night show is also quite popular, so don't miss that either. The second option is island hopping. If you prefer a relaxed tropical vibe, island hopping is the best option. You'll cover multiple islands using speedboards. You can also go snorkeling. You can pre-book this tour using the Klook app. This option is comparatively more peaceful and scenic. Day nine will be a travel day. Take a flight from Phnom Penh to Ho Chi Minh City and then a return flight from Ho Chi Minh City to India. If you have 12 days, you can add Central Vietnam to the nine-day itinerary I've mentioned, starting on Day 6. Return from Sapa to Hanoi on Day 6, then take a flight from Hanoi to Danang. After arriving in Danang, head to the very famous Dragon Bridge in the evening. And if it's a weekend, you can also see a famous fire show there. On Day 7, you can head to Bana Hills in the morning. To reach there, you first need to take a cable car ride, which is quite scenic. The Golden Bridge here is a famous attraction, seemingly supported by joint hands. Within Bana Hills, there's a French village, different themes, rides, cafes, and many other attractions for you to explore. You can also click plenty of Instagram-worthy pictures here. Return to Danang in the evening and visit the Mei Beach, where your entire day's fatigue will be relieved. In the morning of Day 8, you can explore the Marble Mountains or the Santra Peninsula. In the Marble Mountains, you can explore caves, pagodas, temples, and viewpoints. You can also see temples and a statue of Lord Buddha inside the caves. Another option is the Santra Peninsula, famous for its lush greenery and scenic coastal drive. The famous Lady Buddha statue is also located here, creating a truly surreal feel amidst the mountains and ocean. Afterward, you can head to Hoian City, approximately 45 minutes from Da Nang. Hoian is honestly one of Vietnam's prettiest towns. Its lantern streets, riverside cafes, Japanese covered bridges, and yellow-themed buildings give the entire town a truly aesthetic feel. In the evening, when Lantern Street lights up, Hoian appears even more magical. On Day 9, take a flight from Danang to Phuc, and from Day 9 to Day 12, follow the same Phuc itinerary I described in the Day 9 itinerary. If you have 14 days, take a flight from Phuc to Hochiminh City, and your Vietnam trip will be complete. This city is famous for its skyscrapers, rooftop cafes, and modern life. After checking in, you can explore Nguyen, a walking street. This is a very lively area of the city, where you'll find many cafes. You can also visit the famous Cafe Apartment. In the evening, you can enjoy Saigon River, dinner, and cruises. The city skyline lights and live performances give the atmosphere a premium feel. At night, you can visit Bouvien Walking Street, which is famous for Hochiminh City's nightlife. Crowds, lights, and an energetic atmosphere are everywhere. On Day 13, you can combine the Coochie Tunnel and Macon Delta tours. First, you'll visit the Coochie Tunnel. Here, you'll see hidden trapdoors, underground pathways, bunker areas, and wartime survival systems. Some tunnels are so narrow that you have to crawl inside, giving the entire area a historic and intense feel. Afterward, you can explore the Macon Delta region. This area is renowned for its greenery, peaceful vibe, and country-side vibe. Here, you can enjoy coconut candy shops, local fruit tasting, and live folk performances. On Day 14, head to Benthan Market, which is famous for local shopping. You can also buy souvenirs, local products, and coffee there. Afterward, you can explore nearby cafes or simply chill in the city. Depending on your flight timing, you'll head to the airport. The more time you have, the better you can explore Vietnam without rushing too much. If you've found the video useful so far, please support the channel by subscribing. You can visit Vietnam year-round, as the weather in North Central and South Vietnam is quite different. Therefore, the best time depends entirely on which region of Vietnam you want to explore and what type of experience you want. Flights to Vietnamese cities like Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh, and Da Nang are easily available from major cities like Delhi, Mumbai, Bor, and Kolkata. You can set different arrival and departure cities according to your itinerary. For example, I started my trip in Ho Chi Minh and ended in Ho Chi Minh City. If you book your flights two to three months in advance, fare charges can be comparatively lower. The Vietnam visa process is quite simple. You can apply online through the official e-visa portal. The application requires uploading a passport photo and a scan of the passport information page. Ensure your passport is valid for at least six months. Visa approval is usually processed within a few working days. However, I recommend not waiting until the last minute. Internet access becomes crucial upon arrival in Vietnam . Data is required for maps, apps, and Google Translate. Therefore, you can purchase a SIM card at the airport or book one in advance using an app like Klook. If you're traveling in a group, one person can purchase a SIM card, and the rest can purchase theirs in the city. The best network I found is VATL SIM. You can travel between cities in Vietnam. Buses, trains, or flights are practical options. If you have limited time, you can take a flight between cities. Just keep a little buffer time in your itinerary, as weather can cause frequent cancellations and delays. Gab is a great option for traveling within cities. You can also rent scooters if you have an international driving license. All types of accommodations are available in Vietnam, depending on your budget. I usually booked Airbnbs on my trip because they're spacious and have kitchens. You can also use online platforms like airbnb.com, booking.com, or mcmytrip to book accommodations. Vietnam's currency is the Vietnamese Dong. Roughly 1 Indian Rupee = 270 Vietnamese Dong. You can use forex cards like Neo Global Card or Skpia for payments. For a better exchange rate, you can also bring some USD from India. I personally found TP&VP Bank's rates for ATM withdrawals to be much better. Language barriers are common in Vietnam . English isn't widely spoken everywhere, so be sure to download Google Translate before traveling. Vietnam is a paradise for seafood lovers. And if you're a vegetarian, you can try vegetarian banwi or vegetarian hotpot. Indian restaurants are available in major cities, but they're a bit expensive compared to local food. Now let's talk about the overall budget for Vietnam. A round-trip flight can easily cost around 25,000 to 35,000. You can book a decent stage for 1,000 to 2,000 per night. 1,000 per day is sufficient for food. Internal transportation, including domestic flights and buses, will cost around 14,000. Activities and sightseeing will cost 11,000 to 13,000. So, overall, you can easily plan a trip to Vietnam for 70 to 80,000 per person. And if you want to experience a cruise, that will cost an additional 30,000. For a detailed Vietnam experience, check out my Vietnam playlist.
